note — the bold part is what the card te: dreißig is the one ten written with ß; the others end in -zig.
vier + zig: vierzig.
fünf + zig: fünfzig.
The unit comes first, then und, then the ten: one-and-twenty. eins loses its s.
five-and-twenty, written as one word.
fünf und vierzig, in one word. Say the unit first.
zwei und dreißig: zweiunddreißig.
acht und fünfzig. Read long numbers from the back: first the 8, then the 50.
The hour, then Uhr: drei Uhr.
German counts the half towards the next hour: halb vier is half to four, 3:30.
11:30 is halb zwölf: halfway to twelve.
nach: past. Viertel nach zwei is 2:15.
vor: to. Viertel vor zwölf is 11:45.
Minutes, nach, then the hour; Uhr is left out.
fünf vor neun: 8:55.
German asks how late it is: Wie spät ist es?

English: What time is it? – It's **twenty past four**.
German: Wie viel Uhr ist es? – Es ist **zwanzig nach vier**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Wie viel Uhr ist es? is the other way to ask. zwanzig nach vier: 4:20.
Timetables use the 24-hour clock: the hour, Uhr, then the minutes.

German: Der Zug fährt um **acht Uhr dreißig**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The official way: acht Uhr dreißig. In speech, halb neun.

German: Es ist **spät**, und ich bin müde.
note — the bold part is what the card te: spät: late. Es ist spät, with es as the subject, as in English.
um before a clock time: at.

English: The train leaves **at** half past six.
note — the bold part is what the card te: um halb sieben: at 6:30.
um sieben Uhr: at seven o'clock.

English: **At what time** are you coming? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: Um wie viel Uhr…? asks at what time; the whole phrase comes first, then the verb.
am before a day: am Montag. The days are all der-words.
am Dienstag first, so the verb comes second and wir after it.
am Mittwoch: Mittwoch means mid-week.
am Donnerstag, then ist second.
am Freitag: on Friday.
am Samstag, then the verb, then ich.
The subject meine Eltern comes after the verb.

English: **On Sunday at three** my grandma is coming.
German: **Am Sonntag um drei** kommt meine Oma.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The day first, then the time: am Sonntag um drei. Together they take the first place.
After ist, a day takes no article and no am.
am Sonntag goes after the subject in a question.
am Samstag: on Saturday.
nicht comes after am Sonntag, like after heute.
